`You are an expert SEO content writer for Kleza (IT, Development, and Digital Services company).

BLOG TOPIC: ${$json.needDraft[0].Topic}
Focus Keyword: ${$json.needDraft[0]['Focus Keyword']}

STEP 1 – FOCUS KEYWORD RULES (VERY STRICT)

Keyword Density Requirement:
Minimum keyword density = 1%

Approx article length: 800–1000 words → keyword ~10 times

Mandatory placements:
- 1 time in <h1>
- 2 times in first paragraph
- 1 time in at least one <h2>
- 3–4 times in body
- 1 time in CTA

Do NOT exceed 2%.

Use keyword EXACTLY as provided.

---

OVERALL OBJECTIVE:
Write a fully SEO-optimized blog post for Kleza that is ready to publish.

---

CONTENT STRUCTURE REQUIREMENTS:

0️⃣ SEO FIELDS (VERY IMPORTANT)

<!-- SEO_TITLE: ... -->
<!-- SEO_DESCRIPTION: ... -->
<!-- SEO_FOCUS_KEYWORD: ... -->
<!-- SEO_TAGS: ... -->

Rules:
- SEO_TITLE: 55–60 characters
- SEO_DESCRIPTION: 140–160 characters
- Include focus keyword

---

1️⃣ H1
- Exactly one <h1>
- Must include focus keyword

---

2️⃣ INTRODUCTION
- 2 short paragraphs
- Speak to business challenges / digital needs
- Include focus keyword

---

3️⃣ BODY

- Max 3 <h2>
- Use <h3> if needed
- Include:
  - Use cases
  - Benefits
  - Industry insights
  - Practical tips

Include:
- One <ul> list (3–6 points)
- At least 1–2 real-world insights or stats (if relevant)

---

4️⃣ INTERNAL LINKING (KLEZA)

Use these links naturally:

- https://kleza.io/
- https://kleza.io/about-us/
- https://kleza.io/resources/blog/
- https://kleza.io/contact-us/
- https://kleza.io/services/website-development/
- https://kleza.io/services/mobile-app-development/
- https://kleza.io/services/digital-marketing/

Rules:
- Use 3–5 internal links

---

5️⃣ CTA

Include:
- https://kleza.io/contact-us/

Encourage consultation and business growth.

---

OUTPUT FORMAT:

- Clean HTML only
- No markdown
- No explanation

Return ONLY final HTML`
}}

assignments.value: SEO Details SEO Title: Online Reputation Management: Negative Reviews & SEO in 2026 SEO Description: Learn how negative reviews impact SEO and discover essential Online Reputation Management strategies for 2026. Protect your brand's digital image and ranking with Kleza's expert tips. Focus Keyword: Online Reputation Management SEO Tags: Online Reputation Management, SEO, Negative Reviews, Digital Marketing, Brand Reputation, Kleza, ORM  The Impact of Negative Reviews on SEO: Crucial for Online Reputation Management in 2026  Reviews are the building blocks of online marketing. Do you remember scrolling through reviews before buying a new product or even filtering products based on ratings? In today’s digital world, managing these public opinions could be more important for your business than you think. In fact, 97% of the customers say that reviews affect their purchasing decision.  Even a few negative reviews can harm your business faster than the good reviews can build it. They can bring down your rankings, trust factor, and overall SEO. This is why negative feedback needs to be addressed quickly in a proper way. In this blog, we have covered some insightful tips to manage online reputation management after receiving negative reviews. Reviews are not really the issue, but they backfire soon if ignored.  What Negative Reviews Do Behind the Scenes in SEO  Reviews don’t just sit quietly on a page. They start influencing how your business gets seen online. Poor reviews can slowly eat your business by working against search engine visibility. Here’s how they impact: Decreased Trust and Authority   Search engines like Google always prioritize businesses that are trusted by customers. When your business keeps getting a constant wave of negative reviews, it can signal that users don’t find your business reliable. This can lower domain authority and make it even harder to rank for competitive keywords. Reviews also alter customer behavior. Most people don’t think twice before skipping services or products with low ratings. Low Click-Through Rates (CTR)  When your business appears online in search results, the star ratings are often shown with it immediately. A low start rating can repel users from clicking on your website even if your business appears at a high position in search engines. Lower CTA makes your listing less relevant to customers and also leads to a drop in ranking.  Reduced Local SEO Performance  Local search engine optimization is really important for businesses that have physical stores. When people look at your website on platforms like Google My Business or Yelp they can see what customers think of you right away. Poor reviews on such platforms can hurt local rankings and drop a business below competitors who have better ratings. This means that fewer people even know that your business exists locally which automatically means less or no customers.   Proactive Online Reputation Management Strategies for 2026 To build a strong online presence, a proactive approach is required. It is not something that needs to be fixed only once, it is something that needs regular updates through consistent actions.  Some of the key strategies to ace online reputation management are: Strengthen presence on key platforms Your reputation is shaped wherever your brand appears. Make sure your profiles on Google, social media, and review platforms are complete and regularly updated. Incomplete or outdated profiles create doubt, even if your service is good. Let’s look at Domino's Pizza. The brand built a strong digital ecosystem where ordering, tracking, and store information are consistent across all channels. This reduced confusion and made the customer experience smoother, which strengthened trust over time. Improve Brand Trust through Content Reviews help shape how people see a brand. But, they are not the only thing that matters. Keep your website and online profiles updated with content that is easy to understand. A good real life example is Airbnb in its early years. After trust issues around safety and bad user experiences, they improved their content and transparency. They added more details to listings and explained how bookings work in a simpler way. This helped people understand the platform better and slowly rebuild trust over time. Drive positive Feedback The best way to deal with bad reviews is to get a lot of good ones. You can actively encourage satisfied customers to share their experiences on relevant platforms. Follow up after a service or purchase and keep the process simple to leave feedback. A higher volume of positive reviews can reduce the trust factor of negative reviews. Make the timing work in your favour. Ask for feedback when the experience is still fresh so customers respond naturally. You can also use gentle reminders through messages or emails without making it feel forced. Track and Respond Right Away Whether you get positive reviews or negative ones, try not to dismiss them. You can use ORMs like Semrush and Talkwalker to track any feedback across your website. Set a clear internal system so that every review gets a timely response with clear ownership. Also make sure to acknowledge feedback quickly even if the full resolution takes time. This keeps communication active, prevents delays, and helps you manage reputation before small issues grow further. Train teams on customer communication Reputation is not only online. It starts with how customers experience your service at every touchpoint. Train your teams to speak clearly and politely. Ask them to stay calm even in difficult situations. Most negative reviews start with small communication gaps or delays. When your team handles these moments well, many issues stop there itself. Make communication part of daily practice. Keep it consistent across all staff. This builds trust through real interactions and reduces complaints before they reach review platforms. Turn feedback into visible action Collecting feedback is not enough. You need to act on it and show that changes are happening. When customers see improvements based on their input, they feel heard. This strengthens trust more than any promotional message. It also encourages more honest feedback in the future. Review patterns regularly and identify repeated concerns. Fix the root issue instead of handling each complaint separately. Over time, this builds a stronger and more reliable brand image. Ready to Safeguard Your Online Reputation and SEO?  At Kleza Solutions, we understand that your online reputation often shapes how people see your business long before they contact you. A few negative reviews can quietly affect your brand’s reputation and search visibility. This is why we focus on practical support through our wide range of services such as  remote IT, website development, digital marketing, and more. These are designed to keep your brand reputation strong.  Our digital marketing experts create strategic plans that help you manage feedback better and strengthen how your brand is perceived across platforms .Don't let bad reviews hurt your business. Take control with the right online reputation management support and make sure your brand stands out for the right reasons. Get in touch today and start shaping your brand’s story the way it should be seen online.
